chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is travel disliked on any of the disliked days, such as Wednesday and others? He said: 'Begin your journey with charity and recite the Verse of the Throne when it becomes clear to you.'

key_terms.اَلْأَيَّامُ اَلْمَكْرُوهَةُ: disliked days (times recommended to avoid for specific actions)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended acts to perform when beginning a journey according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that travel is not inherently prohibited on disliked days like Wednesday, shifting the focus from superstitious avoidance to spiritual preparation. He prescribes initiating the journey with charity (sadaqah) and reciting Ayat al-Kursi, practices rooted in Shia tradition to invoke divine protection and blessings during travel. This guidance emphasizes proactive piety over passive avoidance of specific times.
